# Change Plan — Adding a Field to `orders-ledger`

**Subject:** adding one new field to the records carried on the `orders-ledger` stream
**Audience:** the stream's owner, as the executing party
**Basis:** the platform's recorded knowledge pages for governed-tier streams (sources listed at the end). Everything below is drawn from those pages; where they are silent, this document says so rather than filling the gap.

---

## 1. Why this stream is not an ordinary change

`orders-ledger` carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from. It is a **governed-tier** stream: its records feed the statutory accounts. The Orders Ledger Stream Runbook is explicit that how it changes is bound by the Governed Tier Obligations "rather than by the producing team's own judgment," and that the governed-tier obligations — not the owner — decide what the owner may approve alone.

Three consequences follow, and they shape the whole plan:

1. **The owner cannot waive the classification** of the change (Governed Tier Obligations).
2. **The owner does not announce the change.** Consumer-facing notices go out centrally through the Change Announcement Directory, which also determines who must hear first (Orders Ledger Stream Runbook).
3. **The owner does not control the timing.** Work on systems feeding the statutory accounts observes the Company Close Calendar, "whose windows are set by the finance organization, not by engineering."

---

## 2. Instruments this change touches

| Code | Instrument | Who owns it | Where it bites |
|---|---|---|---|
| **RB-7** | Change class for incompatible record-shape changes | Change Class Directory | Classification; 17-business-day notice |
| **CM-3** | Compatibility mode (strictest); applies to the orders and settlement streams | Schema Version Register | The proposed version must pass at registration |
| **CA-9** | Per-stream consumer agreement | Consumer Agreement Ledger | Who is owed notice; whose fields are affected |
| **AN-5** | Change bulletin | Change Announcement Directory | The announcement itself |
| **RR-21** | Filing series for issued circulars and bulletins | Corporate Records Retention Directory | Filing the bulletin with delivery evidence |
| **QW-4** | Quiet window (journal cutoff → statement sign-off) | Company Close Calendar | When the change may be applied |
| **AT-12** | Owner attestation | Attestation Procedure | Closing the change |
| **EG-24 / SA-27** | Off-platform copy approval / covering instrument | Off-platform Copy Policy; Data Sharing Agreement Register | Only if output leaves the platform (see §11) |
| **CE-2 / PM-6 / TL-19** | Incident closure evidence / review record / worked-hours entry | Closure Evidence Standard; Review Record Standard; Worked Hours Ledger Practice | Contingency path only (see §12) |

---

## 3. Step 1 — Classify the change, before any work begins

Governed Tier Obligations: "Every change to what a governed stream carries is classified before any work begins." Classification precedes design work, code, and scheduling — not just deployment.

**How this change classifies.** The Change Class Directory places **a field added** explicitly within class **RB-7**, alongside renamed, retyped and removed fields. The same page's "Other classes" paragraph says compatible additions carry the lighter classes, which owe an announcement but no waiting period. A new field can be argued into either description, so the directory's own tie-breaker governs:

> "When in doubt between two classes, the heavier one applies until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing."

**Therefore:**

- **Plan on RB-7 as the operative class.** This is the default, and it is the class the rest of this plan is built around.
- A lighter class becomes available **only** on written agreement from the owner of the consuming side. Verbal agreement, silence, or the producing team's own assessment of the change as small does not qualify — the directory states the class "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small: compatibility is judged from the consumer's side."
- Whatever is decided, **the owner cannot waive the classification** (Governed Tier Obligations). Downgrading is a consuming-side act recorded in writing, not an owner's call.

**Deliverable of this step:** a recorded classification of RB-7 (or a lighter class plus the written consuming-side agreements that justify it), available to be carried into the register entry, which records "the classification of the change that produced it."

---

## 4. Step 2 — Draft the proposal against the registered schema

The Orders Ledger Stream Runbook: any change to the record shape "starts with a proposal against the stream's registered schema; versions and their compatibility standing live in" the Schema Version Register.

The proposal must carry enough to survive the CM-3 check in Step 3 and to populate the register entry:

- The current registered version of `orders-ledger` as the baseline.
- The new field: name, type, and whether it is optional or required on the record.
- The behaviour of the field on records the producer cannot populate.
- The classification from Step 1.
- The proposed new version identifier.

*The recorded material does not specify a proposal form, template, or submission venue.* See Open items.

---

## 5. Step 3 — Pass the CM-3 compatibility check

The Schema Version Register states that each stream declares a compatibility mode and **every proposed version is checked against that mode at registration time**. `orders-ledger` is one of the orders and settlement streams, which "sit in mode **CM-3**, the strictest":

> "A new version must be readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change."

This is the substantive engineering constraint on the field's design, and it is stricter than "the field is additive." Test the proposal against it directly:

- Every consumer reading the previous version must be able to read a record carrying the new field **without changing its code**. Consumers that fail on unknown fields, or that validate records against a closed shape, fail this test.
- "Every consumer of the previous one" is measured against the CA-9 register of consumers (§6), not against the consumers the producing team happens to know about.
- The check is performed **at registration time**, so a proposal that cannot pass it does not become a registered version and no producer may write it.

If the proposed field cannot satisfy CM-3, the change does not proceed in this form. The recorded material offers no exception route for CM-3 — unlike QW-4, which has a written-exception path — so treat CM-3 as a hard gate.

---

## 6. Step 4 — Review the consumer agreements

The Consumer Agreement Ledger records who consumes each governed stream and under what agreement. Each consuming team registers a **CA-9** agreement per stream naming **the consuming service, its owner, and the fields it depends on**. Two properties of the ledger matter here:

**It is the notice boundary.** "Announcements are delivered to registered consumers, and a team that never registered is owed nothing, however long it has been reading." Registration is also a condition of read access. The owner's obligation runs to the ledger's list — not to a list of teams believed to be reading.

**Agreements are reviewed when a stream's shape changes.** Pull every CA-9 agreement against `orders-ledger` and, for each, compare its declared dependent fields against the change. The ledger then grants a discretion:

> "A consumer whose declared fields are untouched by a change may be notified without being waited for, at the announcing owner's discretion."

**How to apply that discretion here — and the caution attached.** A pure field addition touches no existing declared field, so on a literal reading every registered consumer qualifies to be notified-without-being-waited-for, which would empty the RB-7 waiting period of content. That sits badly against two other recorded rules: the class "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small," and the owner "cannot waive a classification." The recorded material does not resolve which rule prevails when the discretion is exercised across the whole consumer list at once.

**Recommended course:** serve the full RB-7 notice period (§8) as the default, and exercise the CA-9 discretion only for consumers whose owner has *also* agreed in writing — which is the same written agreement the Change Class Directory requires for a lighter class. This satisfies both pages under either reading. Record the decision for each consumer, with the written agreement attached where one was relied on. The unresolved interaction is listed under Open items and is worth adjudicating with whoever maintains the Change Class Directory before you rely on the discretion at scale.

**Deliverable:** a per-consumer table — service, owner, declared fields, affected yes/no, waited-for yes/no, and the basis for any not-waited-for entry.

---

## 7. Step 5 — Register the new version

Register the version in the Schema Version Register. Two rules bind the timing:

- **"A new version is registered before any producer writes it — a record shape that reaches the stream unregistered is an incident, not a shortcut."** Registration precedes any production write of the new shape, including a partial or trial one.
- Registration is when the CM-3 check happens (§5).

The register entry carries **the version, the classification of the change that produced it, and who approved it**, and entries are "the authoritative answer to 'what changed and when'."

Register **before** the announcement, because the AN-5 bulletin is posted against the stream's register entry (§8) and so requires the entry to exist.

*The recorded material names no approver role for a registered version, and does not say whether registration is itself an approval step with a separate approving party or a record of an approval given elsewhere.* See Open items.

---

## 8. Step 6 — Have the AN-5 bulletin issued, and start the clock

**The owner does not issue this.** The Change Announcement Directory: "Consumer-facing change notices are issued centrally so no consumer's notice depends on which team is making the change." The Orders Ledger Stream Runbook repeats it: "Nothing is announced by the producing team directly."

The announcement is an **AN-5 bulletin**, and it is:

- **Delivered to every consumer the stream's agreement ledger lists** — the CA-9 list from §6.
- **Posted against the stream's register entry.** The posted copy is authoritative: "the authoritative copy when a delivered copy and the register disagree." If a consumer later disputes what was announced, the register entry governs, not the copy in their inbox.

**Filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought.** Bulletin issues are corporate correspondence and their retention "is not the announcing team's decision." Under the Corporate Records Retention Directory, issued bulletins belong to **series RR-21** (issued circulars and bulletins), and items in the series "are filed with their delivery evidence at the time of issue." Disposal is reviewed by the records office, not by the issuing or announcing team.

That delivery evidence is not merely a records-office formality — it is what fixes the start of the notice period, so confirm it is captured at issue.

### The notice period

Class RB-7 owes consumers **17 business days of advance notice before the change is applied**. Two qualifications:

- **The clock runs from the day the announcement is actually delivered** — not the day it was drafted, approved, or posted.
- **The days are counted in the consuming teams' working calendar**, not the producing team's. Where consumers sit on different calendars, the count is per-consumer and the change waits for the last one.

The Change Class Directory's own summary describes what a class owes consumers "before work may begin," while its body sets the 17 days as advance notice "before the change is applied." Where these differ, the conservative course is to have the bulletin issued before implementation work begins **and** to hold the application of the change until at least 17 business days after delivery.

*A worked set of dates cannot be given here: the consuming teams and their working calendars are not recorded on the platform.* See Open items.

---

## 9. Step 7 — Apply the change, subject to the quiet window

Two independent gates must both be open before the field goes live.

**Gate 1 — the RB-7 notice period has elapsed** for every consumer being waited for (§8).

**Gate 2 — the change is outside QW-4.** The Company Close Calendar defines the stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off as the **QW-4 quiet window**. During QW-4:

> "Systems whose figures flow into the statements are left as they are: production alterations to those systems wait until the books are signed, because an alteration mid-close turns every reconciliation difference into a question about the alteration."

`orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, so it is squarely within scope. The close sequence is journal cutoff → subledger agreement → consolidation → sign-off of the statements; between cutoff and sign-off the control group's attention is on agreement of balances, not new activity.

- **Check the current window's standing before scheduling.** Period dates, cutoff times, and the current window's standing "are published on the finance group's internal page each period." Check that page for the specific period you are targeting rather than assuming a fixed monthly shape — the calendar runs on a working-day cadence the controller publishes, which can move.
- **Exceptions exist but are costly.** "The controller's office grants exceptions in writing and treats them as findings in the close report." An exception is available if the change genuinely cannot wait; it is not a way to save a few days.
- **This window is not the owner's to set.** Governed Tier Obligations: change timing "does not belong to the producing team alone."

**Also observe the stream's own rhythm.** The Orders Ledger Stream Runbook records that the stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning. Schedule the application so the change lands cleanly against the overnight settlement and the next morning's lag review, and so the "first full settlement" required for attestation (§10) follows promptly.

**Do not write the new shape before its version is registered.** A record shape reaching the stream unregistered is an incident (§12), and that includes writing the new field ahead of the notice period or ahead of registration.

---

## 10. Step 8 — Attest, and only then is the change finished

The Attestation Procedure closes the change. The producing service's owner files form **AT-12**.

**When:** "once the change is live **and the first full settlement has passed**." Not at deploy time — a full settlement cycle must complete first, which for this stream means the overnight settlement window described in the runbook.

**What it states:**

1. The records now flowing match the registered version.
2. No consumer-visible field was dropped along the way.
3. The announced scope is the delivered scope.

Point 3 is the one to watch on a change like this: if the field's name, type, or nullability shifted between the AN-5 bulletin and what actually shipped, the announced scope is no longer the delivered scope. Either the delivered change must be brought back to the announced scope, or the announcement must be re-issued — which restarts the RB-7 clock, since the notice runs from actual delivery.

**Who signs:** "The signature is personal to the owner: it cannot be delegated below the service's named owner." Note the sharp consequence recorded for a gap in that role: **"a vacancy in that role suspends changes rather than the attestation."** If the named owner post is vacant, this change does not proceed; the attestation obligation is not what gives way.

**If it is not filed:** "An unattested change stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every review until the form is filed." Governed Tier Obligations puts it more bluntly: an unattested change is "treated as unfinished however long it has been live." The field being in production is not the end of the plan; AT-12 is.

---

## 11. Conditional obligation — off-platform copies

This applies only if output carrying the new field is copied outside the platform. It is not triggered by the field addition on its own, but a new field can invalidate an existing arrangement, so check it.

- **EG-24 approval.** No feed output leaves the platform on an operator's judgment alone. Every copy outside the platform carries an EG-24 approval naming the receiving party, the purpose, and the date the copy will be deleted; an approval missing any of the three "is returned unactioned," and the approval is filed **before** the copy is made. Re-copies run under an existing approval "only while the purpose and recipient are unchanged."
- **SA-27 covering instrument.** The approval must cite the agreement making the transfer lawful, looked up in the legal office's Data Sharing Agreement Register. An SA-27 entry records the counterparty, **the categories of records covered**, the permitted purposes, and the instrument's expiry. Crucially, "the citation is checked against the entry's categories and purposes, not against the transferring team's intent."

**The check to run:** if the new field introduces a category of record not covered by the existing SA-27 entry behind any current off-platform copy, that copy is no longer covered once the field is live. "An expired or absent instrument means the transfer waits for the legal office, however routine the request." Raise this with the legal office ahead of go-live, not after — the register "is the only authoritative list," and team-held copies of instruments are working copies whose dates do not govern.

---

## 12. Contingency — if an unregistered shape reaches the stream

The Schema Version Register is unambiguous that a record shape reaching the stream unregistered "is an incident, not a shortcut." If that happens — a producer writes the new field before registration, or ships a shape that differs from the registered one — the change stops being a change and becomes an incident.

The closure standards recorded on the platform describe **control-failure** incident handling. *The material does not state that an unregistered-shape incident is a control-failure incident, so whether these standards govern it is not established here* (see Open items). Recorded for the owner's use, that path is:

1. **CE-2 evidence record (Closure Evidence Standard).** "A control-failure incident closes on evidence, not on silence." Closure requires the control passing **on its own schedule, unassisted**, with the previously unagreed days brought current. "A manually forced pass does not qualify — the record must come from the scheduled run itself — and a quiet night with the control disabled qualifies even less." The CE-2 record is attached to the incident **before** the closing notice goes out.
2. **PM-6 review record (Review Record Standard).** Every closed control-failure incident files one. It carries a timeline of the nights in question, the originating conditions as actually understood, the corrections to be made **with a named owner for each**, and the review meeting's outcome. "A record whose corrections have no owner is returned to the incident's owner rather than filed." It is filed against the incident and referenced from the control's own operating notes. It is due on the standard's own clock, not at closure time.
3. **TL-19 hours (Worked Hours Ledger Practice).** Hours worked outside the working day on those nights are entered by hand under code TL-19 with the date and a one-line purpose, **before the payroll cutoff of the following week**, and before the PM-6 record is filed. "An unentered line lapses — the ledger closes with payroll, and a late claim reopens nothing." A correction to a closed period becomes a payroll correction applied on the following run, adjusting pay and never the closed ledger.

The practical instruction: register first (§7). The cost of the shortcut is an incident file, an evidence record that cannot be manufactured, a review record with owned corrections, and a payroll-clock deadline on the people who worked the nights.

---

## 13. Execution checklist

| # | Step | Gate that must be satisfied | Who acts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Classify the change | Before any work begins; RB-7 unless consuming-side owners agree lighter **in writing**; owner cannot waive | Owner *(classifying party not recorded)* |
| 2 | Draft the proposal against the registered schema | Baseline is the current registered version | Owner |
| 3 | Pass the CM-3 check | Readable by every previous-version consumer **without a code change**; checked at registration | Schema Version Register |
| 4 | Review CA-9 agreements | Every registered consumer identified; affected-fields comparison done | Owner |
| 5 | Register the new version | **Before any producer writes the shape**; before the bulletin | Schema Version Register *(approver not recorded)* |
| 6 | Have the AN-5 bulletin issued | Issued centrally, not by the producing team; delivered to all CA-9 consumers; posted against the register entry; filed under RR-21 with delivery evidence at issue | Central announcement function + records office |
| 7 | Wait out the notice | 17 business days from **actual delivery**, in the **consuming teams'** calendar | — |
| 8 | Confirm the close window | Outside QW-4, per the finance group's page for that period; written controller exception otherwise (a close-report finding) | Controller's office |
| 9 | Apply the change | Both gates open; aligned to the overnight settlement and morning lag review | Owner / producing team |
| 10 | Check off-platform coverage, if any | EG-24 approval filed before any copy; SA-27 categories still cover the new field | Owner + legal office |
| 11 | File AT-12 | Change live **and first full settlement passed**; signed personally by the named owner | Named service owner |

---

## 14. What consumers are owed, in one place

1. **Registration as the entry ticket.** CA-9 registration is a condition of read access and the notice boundary. Registered consumers get everything below; a team that never registered "is owed nothing, however long it has been reading."
2. **An AN-5 bulletin, issued centrally**, delivered to them by name from the agreement ledger — never an ad-hoc note from the producing team.
3. **A version they can read without changing their code**, guaranteed by the CM-3 check at registration, not by the producer's assurance.
4. **17 business days of advance notice** before the change is applied, counted in *their* working calendar, running from the day the bulletin was actually delivered — unless their own owner has agreed otherwise in writing.
5. **An authoritative record they can appeal to.** The bulletin posted against the register entry governs over any delivered copy; the register entry is the authoritative statement of what changed, when, under what classification, and who approved it.
6. **A filed, retained bulletin with delivery evidence**, under series RR-21, retained and disposed of on the records office's terms rather than the announcing team's.
7. **A signed AT-12 attestation** that the records now flowing match the registered version, that nothing consumer-visible was dropped, and that what was announced is what was delivered.
8. **A review of their agreement** when the shape changes, with an explicit decision recorded on whether they were waited for.

---

# Incident Handling Document — Settlement-Recon Nightly Job, Third Consecutive Failed Night

**Status:** active procedure, for the on-shift engineer
**Prepared:** 2026-08-10
**Trigger condition:** the nightly settlement-recon job has failed on three consecutive nights
**Grounded in:** the platform's knowledge pages for this control (cited in full at the end)

---

## 1. Why this is now an incident

The nightly settlement-recon job agrees the day's settlement records against the processor statements. A clean pass is silent; a failed pass leaves the day unagreed and is re-attempted the following night after the upstream statements refresh.

The runbook grades failures by count, and the count you have is the formal one:

| Nights failed | Standing |
|---|---|
| One | Watched. No record. |
| Two | Worked during the day. No record. |
| **Three consecutive** | **No longer an operational matter — an incident record is opened.** |

The reason the third night is the threshold is that the unagreed days now span a statement cycle. That is also the fact that drives the severity band, so state it in the record explicitly rather than describing the failure only as "job failing."

The runbook is deliberate that its own scope ends at opening the record honestly. Everything after that point is governed by the standards below, not by the job's operators and not by your judgment on the night.

---

## 2. What is opened, and at what severity

**Open an IN-28 incident record.** This is the record type the runbook names for a third consecutive failed night.

**Severity: band SB-8.** A reconciliation or settlement control failing across a statement cycle is band SB-8. Two things follow from how the standard is written, and both matter on the night:

- **Severity is assigned when the record is opened.** It is not deferred, not provisional, and not revised once someone senior looks at it.
- **Severity belongs to the standard, not to the team that opened it.** You do not have discretion to open this lower because the cause looks small, because a fix is in hand, or because the days may agree tomorrow. The lighter bands cover single-night failures and non-control degradations; this is neither.

Band SB-8 determines two downstream things automatically: who is notified at opening (§3) and which escalation route the incident climbs (§5).

**In the record, at opening, state at minimum:** that the control is settlement-recon; that it has failed three consecutive nights; the three nights by date; that the unagreed days span a statement cycle; the assigned band (SB-8); and the update cadence you are promising under §6.

---

## 3. Who has to be told at opening

Band SB-8 notifies, at opening:

1. **The owning team** for the settlement-recon job.
2. **The platform group's shift lead.**

Both are notified at opening — this is not a sequence where the shift lead is a fallback for the owning team. The shift lead notification is also the first rung of the escalation route, so it starts the clock in §5 whether or not anyone acts on it.

*The material available here does not name the owning team for settlement-recon, and the escalation roster gives roles rather than people or contact channels. Identify the owning team from the job's own ownership record before you send anything, and record who you notified and at what time — the escalation clocks are measured from those timestamps.*

### 3a. Compliance office — the notification that is not the engineering organization's to schedule

Bands touching settlement controls carry one further obligation. **When the failure falls inside a statutory filing window, notification follows the Regulatory Filing Calendar, which the compliance office maintains.** You will not be able to determine from platform material whether today falls inside such a window; the calendar is the compliance office's, published a year ahead, naming each filing, its lodgment date, and the in-scope arrangements it draws on.

Therefore, on the night:

- **Ask the compliance office, in writing, whether the affected days fall inside an open filing window and whether settlement-recon is on the in-scope list for that filing.** The office confirms scope questions in writing within a working day.
- If the answer is yes, the filing carries **form RN-26**: lodged with the filing, before the window closes, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand.
- **Timing is the whole point of this step.** The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open. Word arriving after lodgment becomes a correction, which the regulators treat differently. Do not hold this question until the incident is understood, and do not hold it until business hours if a window may be open and near lodgment — ask now, and note the ask and its timestamp in the incident record.
- Note also that the office's attention during a window belongs to the filing, not to new requests. Expect the written confirmation on the working-day clock, not immediately, and do not let the wait stall §5.

---

## 4. What to do about the job itself while the incident is open

**The job keeps running on its schedule.** Do not disable, pause, or suppress it to quiet the alerting. A quiet night with the control disabled is explicitly disqualified as closure evidence (§7), so switching it off does not merely fail to help — it removes the only route to closing the incident.

**On repair by re-run.** A separate procedure, RP-22, governs repairing a nightly feed's bad night: affected write-date partitions are replaced whole, under the feed's own prefix, and the original write date stays the partition's identity, so a re-run performed days later still lands under the night it repairs. A re-run that would change a partition's write date is not a re-run and the layout forbids it. Re-runs happen only after the upstream collectors have drained for the affected window; re-running ahead of the upstream repair reproduces the bad night. *RP-22 is written for nightly feeds and is not referenced by the settlement-recon runbook, so treat its applicability to this job as unconfirmed — check with the owning team before performing a re-run under it.* Whatever repair is performed, note §7: a forced or manual pass does not close the incident.

---

## 5. Escalation, and the clocks that run when nobody responds

Band SB-8 escalates along the **garnet route**. Severity decides the route; the roster decides the names.

**The garnet route, in order:**

| Rung | Role | Acknowledgment clock |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Platform shift lead | **23 minutes** |
| 2 | Duty manager | **34 minutes** |
| 3 | Head of platform operations | **Holds until answered** — there is nowhere further to climb |

*The clock table records these as the clocks for "the settlement family of routes." Garnet is the route this band assigns for a settlement control failure, so these are the clocks that apply; if you find a garnet-specific entry that differs, that entry wins.*

**How the climb behaves — rule AC-15:**

- **A rung is climbed one at a time.** An escalation never skips a rung that has acknowledged.
- **A clock that runs out without an acknowledgment advances the call to the next rung on its own.** You do not have to push it, and you should not wait to be asked.
- **A missed rung is recorded as missed, not retried.** Do not re-page a rung whose clock expired in the hope of catching them the second time. It is recorded as missed and the call has moved on.
- **Acknowledging stops the climb at that rung.**
- **Declining passes the call upward immediately,** without waiting out the remainder of the clock.
- **The final rung holds until answered.** If the head of platform operations has not answered, the escalation is still live and still yours to keep alive; there is no expiry that releases it.

**Worked example of a fully unanswered night.** The record opens at 02:00 and the shift lead is notified. No acknowledgment by 02:23 — the shift lead rung is recorded as missed and the call advances to the duty manager. No acknowledgment by 02:57 — the duty manager rung is recorded as missed and the call advances to the head of platform operations, where it stays open until answered.

**An escalation in flight finishes on the roster it started on.** If the roster is edited mid-incident, your escalation continues on the rungs it began with. (Routes change only by agreement between the owning teams and the platform group, in writing, before the roster is edited.)

---

## 6. What is communicated while the incident is open

Cadence **UC-11** applies to control-failure incidents.

**The opening notice must name:**

- the affected control (settlement-recon);
- the days in question (the three unagreed nights);
- **when the next update will arrive.**

**The cadence is a promise.** The interval is the one your opening notice declared, and once declared it binds. **Missing an update is itself reportable.** Choose an interval you can meet through the quiet hours rather than an ambitious one — an honest longer interval is compliant, a missed short one is not.

**Every subsequent update either reports progress or re-promises the next update time honestly.** "Nothing to report" is an acceptable update; silence is not, and neither is letting a promised time slide without a new promise.

**Audience is fixed.** Updates go to the same audience as the opening notice — that is, the owning team and the platform shift lead per §3, plus anyone the notice included. **Narrowing the audience mid-incident is not permitted, however quiet the update.** Do not drop recipients once the incident goes uneventful, and do not move the conversation into a smaller channel.

**The closing notice is part of the standard.** It goes to the full audience and **names the evidence the closure rests on** (§7).

---

## 7. What has to be true before the incident can be closed

**A control-failure incident closes on evidence, not on silence.**

Closure requires a **CE-2 evidence record**, and the standard is specific about what qualifies:

- **The control passes on its own schedule** — the record must come from the scheduled run itself.
- **Unassisted** — a manually forced pass does not qualify.
- **With the previously unagreed days brought current** — a pass that succeeds only for the current day, leaving the three nights unagreed, is not closure evidence.
- **A quiet night with the control disabled qualifies even less.** Absence of failure is not evidence of a pass.

**The CE-2 record is attached to the incident before the closing notice goes out.** The order is: scheduled unassisted pass with the days brought current → CE-2 record attached to the incident → closing notice to the full audience naming that evidence → incident closed.

Nothing else closes it: not a fix merged, not a cause identified, not the owning team's confidence, not the passage of time.

---

## 8. The record the incident has to leave behind

Closure is not the end of the obligation. **Every closed control-failure incident files a PM-6 review record.**

**PM-6 carries:**

1. **A timeline of the nights in question.**
2. **The originating conditions as they are actually understood** — as understood, not as first assumed and not tidied into a cleaner story than the evidence supports.
3. **The corrections that will be made, with a named owner for each.** Owned corrections are tracked to completion. **A record whose corrections have no owner is returned to the incident's owner rather than filed** — an unassigned correction will bounce the whole record back.
4. **The review meeting's outcome.**

**Where it is filed:** against the incident, **and referenced from the control's own operating notes** — that is, from the Settlement Recon Job Runbook — so the next operator to meet the same failure finds what this one learned. Both placements are required; filing against the incident alone leaves the runbook unimproved.

**Timing:** the review record is **due on the review standard's own clock, not at closure time.** Do not treat closing the incident as discharging it.

### 8a. The people side — worked hours

**Before the PM-6 record is filed, the hours spent on the nights in question are entered in the worked-hours ledger,** because the workforce office's ledger closes on its own rhythm whether or not the review is done.

For each person who worked these nights:

- Ordinary working-day hours flow into the ledger from badge records automatically and need no attention.
- **Hours worked outside the working day are entered by hand under code TL-19,** with the date and a one-line purpose, **before the payroll cutoff of the following week.**
- **An unentered line lapses.** The ledger closes with payroll and a late claim reopens nothing.
- Entered TL-19 hours accrue toward time off in lieu at the rate the employment terms set; the balance shows beside leave in the workforce portal.
- If a period has already closed, the fix is a payroll correction: the payroll administrators apply it on the following run and it adjusts pay, never the closed ledger. Questions about a closed period go to the workforce office in writing and are answered against the ledger as it closed.

Because the incident's nights are already three deep and the payroll cutoff runs on its own calendar, **prompt the people who worked these nights to enter their TL-19 lines now, not when the review is scheduled.**

---

## 9. Sequence for the on-shift engineer

1. Confirm the third consecutive failed night and record the three dates.
2. Open the **IN-28** record at band **SB-8**. Do not adjust the band.
3. Notify the **owning team** and the **platform shift lead**. Timestamp both.
4. Send the **opening notice** under **UC-11**: control, days, and when the next update arrives.
5. Ask the **compliance office in writing** whether the affected days fall inside an open statutory filing window and whether settlement-recon is in scope; if yes, **RN-26** is lodged before that window closes.
6. Leave the job **running on its schedule**. Do not disable or force it.
7. Run the **garnet** escalation: shift lead (23 min) → duty manager (34 min) → head of platform operations (holds until answered). Expired clocks advance on their own; missed rungs are recorded, not retried; a decline advances immediately.
8. Keep the promised update cadence, to the **full unchanged audience**, until closure.
9. Close only on a **CE-2** record: scheduled, unassisted pass with the unagreed days brought current. Attach it, then send the closing notice naming it.
10. Get **TL-19** hours entered before the payroll cutoff of the following week.
11. File the **PM-6** review record — timeline, originating conditions as understood, owned corrections, meeting outcome — against the incident and referenced from the settlement-recon runbook.

# invoice-adjustments — Feed Onboarding Document

**Status:** onboarding draft, prepared 2026-08-10
**Model feed:** `parcel-events` — this feed is to be operated exactly as that one is
**Basis:** the operating standards recorded on this platform and reached from the *Parcel Events Feed Runbook*

---

## 1. Purpose and scope

`invoice-adjustments` is a new nightly feed to be stood up and operated on the same terms as `parcel-events`. This document states, for each area of its operation, the standard that governs it and what that standard requires of this feed.

An important point of principle carried over from the model feed: almost nothing that makes `parcel-events` operable lives in the feed's own runbook. Its operability lives in the platform-wide standards it follows. The same is true here — this document does not create feed-specific rules where a standard already applies; it records which standard applies and what obligation it places on `invoice-adjustments`.

The `parcel-events` runbook also records a dependency rule that shapes how the feed is operated: it runs only after its upstream collectors drain, and a missing hour in the output is an upstream matter that a re-run cannot repair, because a re-run cannot supply records the upstream never delivered. The equivalent upstream for `invoice-adjustments` is not recorded on this platform; see Open items.

---

## 2. How the feed and its output are named

Governed by the **Feed Naming Standard**, pattern **FN-13**.

- A feed's name is its contract with everyone who schedules against it.
- Names under FN-13 are formed as **the subject first, then the grain of the records, joined with a dash**. `parcel-events` is the standard's own worked example of the pattern.
- The name `invoice-adjustments` conforms to FN-13 as given: subject `invoice`, grain `adjustments`, dash-joined.
- **The output carries the feed's name.** A consumer must never need a lookup table to connect the feed to its output. So the output of this feed is identified as `invoice-adjustments` — the same token used for the feed itself, and (see §3) the same token that names its prefix in the landing zone.

### If the feed is ever renamed

A rename runs through an **alias period**:

1. The old name keeps working while registered consumers move over.
2. The alias is retired **only when the delivery records show no reads against it** — not on a calendar date, and not on the feed team's assertion that consumers have moved.
3. Renaming without an alias period is not a rename. It is treated as decommissioning one feed and launching another, with every obligation that carries.

---

## 3. Where the output lands, and how that area is organized

Governed by the **Landing Zone Layout**, layout **LZ-14**.

- **One feed, one prefix.** `invoice-adjustments` owns exactly one prefix in the landing area, and that prefix is named for the feed. Under LZ-14 combined with FN-13, the prefix is therefore `invoice-adjustments`.
- **Everything the feed writes lands under that prefix, partitioned by write date.** There is no second location for any part of the output.
- **Nothing writes outside its own prefix.** If `invoice-adjustments` turns out to need a second area, that is not a second prefix for one feed — under LZ-14 it is two feeds, and the second one is named, registered, declared and operated in its own right.
- **Nothing but the feed writes inside the prefix.** The point of the rule is that ownership of any object in the landing zone is readable from its path alone.
- **Consumers read; consumers do not write.** No consumer may place markers, checkpoints or scratch output inside the `invoice-adjustments` prefix. Consumer state lives with the consumer.

The absolute root of the landing area (bucket, container or filesystem root) is not recorded on this platform; the standard specifies the organization of the zone, not its address. See Open items.

---

## 4. How its storage is registered, and how long its output lives

Governed by the **Storage Tier Register**, tier **ST-16**, with capacity accounted through the **Procurement Commitment Ledger**, line **PV-25**.

### Registration

- Every feed registers its output in **exactly one** storage tier, and the tier — not the feed team — decides the output's lifetime.
- **Nightly operational feeds register in tier ST-16.** `parcel-events` sits in ST-16, and the register states directly that a feed operated like it registers there too. `invoice-adjustments` therefore registers in **ST-16**.

### Lifetime of the output

- **Output in ST-16 is purged 47 days after its write date.** This is the retention that applies to `invoice-adjustments` output.
- Keeping anything longer than 47 days is **not** an extension the feed team can grant. It is a **re-registration into a retention tier**, and it is reviewed by the register's owners. If any consumer of `invoice-adjustments` needs data older than 47 days, that requirement must go to the register's owners as a re-registration before the feed is relied on for it — not be handled by the feed team holding output back.

### Capacity

Registration is also the moment capacity is accounted for:

- Platform storage is bought ahead under standing vendor commitments held by the **procurement office**. A new registration **draws against line PV-25**, the standing commitment for bulk storage.
- **Registering the feed is what makes the draw visible to procurement.** Draws are recorded as internal registrations are made, and the office sizes each renewal from the recorded draws — **an unrecorded draw is capacity the renewal will not cover.**
- **New draws are confirmed with the vendor manager before they begin.** Standing up `invoice-adjustments` is a new draw, so this confirmation is a prerequisite of the feed writing, not a follow-up.
- A draw that would take PV-25 past its committed volume **waits for the renewal** rather than assuming it. Renewals run on the procurement office's own negotiation calendar.
- If `invoice-adjustments` is expected to be a **large** draw, the ledger's instruction is to talk to the procurement office **a cycle ahead** of the negotiation calendar. The expected volume of this feed is not recorded; see Open items.

---

## 5. When the output is expected to land, and what happens when it is repeatedly late

Governed by the **Delivery Expectation Standard**, table **LH-18**.

### Declaring the landing hour

- Every nightly feed **declares its expected landing hour in table LH-18**, and that declaration is what consumers schedule against.
- **An undeclared feed has no lateness, only unpredictability.** Declaring an hour for `invoice-adjustments` in LH-18 is therefore part of standing it up, not an optional refinement — until it is declared, the feed cannot be said to be late, and consumers have nothing legitimate to schedule against.

The specific hour to declare for `invoice-adjustments` is not determined by this document; no landing hour for this feed, and no LH-18 value for `parcel-events`, is recorded on this platform. See Open items.

### Lateness

- A feed landing **after its declared hour is late**, and lateness is tracked **per morning** against the declaration.
- **One late morning is noted.**
- **Repeated late mornings in the same week are raised with the owning team as a delivery matter.** The matter has exactly two acceptable resolutions:
  1. **The window moves and the declaration is corrected**, or
  2. **the cause is fixed.**

  Chronic lateness that is neither corrected in LH-18 nor fixed at the cause is not a third option.
- **Quietly re-declaring a later hour to absorb lateness is prohibited.** Moving the declared hour is a change consumers must be told about like any other change.

---

## 6. How it is re-run safely after a bad night

Governed by the **Feed Re-run Procedure**, procedure **RP-22**.

- **A re-run repairs a bad night by replacing it, never by appending to it.**
- The affected **write-date partitions are replaced whole**, under the feed's own prefix (`invoice-adjustments`, per §3). Partial patching or additive correction is not a re-run.
- **The original write date stays the partition's identity.** A re-run performed days later still lands under the night it repairs, so consumers re-reading that partition see the corrected records exactly where the bad ones were.
- **A re-run that would change a partition's write date is not a re-run.** It is a new feed writing into an old feed's zone, and the landing zone layout (LZ-14) forbids it.
- **Sequencing:** re-runs happen **after the upstream collectors have drained for the affected window.** Re-running ahead of the upstream repair simply reproduces the bad night.
- Following from the model feed's operating note: if the defect is a **missing** window rather than a wrong one, a re-run is not the remedy at all — a re-run cannot supply records the upstream never delivered. That is an upstream matter to be repaired upstream first, after which the re-run replaces the affected partitions.

---

## 7. What applies if any of its output is copied outside the platform

Governed by the **Off-platform Copy Policy**, approval **EG-24**, citing the **Data Sharing Agreement Register**, entry type **SA-27**.

### The controlling rule

**No feed output leaves the platform on an operator's judgment alone.** This applies to any copy of `invoice-adjustments` output taken outside the platform, by anyone, for any purpose.

### The EG-24 approval

Every off-platform copy carries an **EG-24 approval** naming three things:

1. **the receiving party**,
2. **the purpose**, and
3. **the date the copy will be deleted**.

An approval missing any of the three is **returned unactioned**. The approval is **filed before the copy is made**.

**Re-copies:** a further copy under an existing approval counts as a re-copy **only while the purpose and the recipient are unchanged**. A new recipient or a new purpose is a new approval, not a re-copy.

### The covering instrument

An EG-24 approval must also **cite the agreement that makes the transfer lawful**:

- The covering instrument is looked up in the **Data Sharing Agreement Register**, maintained by the **legal office**.
- Each instrument is an **SA-27 entry** recording the **counterparty**, the **categories of records covered**, the **permitted purposes**, and the **instrument's expiry**.
- The citation is **checked against the entry's categories and purposes — not against the transferring team's intent.** It is not enough that the feed team considers a transfer routine or in-scope; the SA-27 entry has to actually cover the record category and the purpose.
- **A transfer with no instrument to cite does not proceed, whatever its purpose.** An expired or absent instrument means the transfer **waits for the legal office**, however routine the request.
- **The register is the only authoritative list.** Copies of instruments held by teams are working copies, and **the register's expiry dates govern.**

Whether any current SA-27 entry covers the category of records `invoice-adjustments` will carry is not recorded on this platform, and is not something the feed team may assume. See Open items.

---

## 8. Standards this feed is operated under

|---|---|---|---|
| Model feed | Parcel Events Feed Runbook | — | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_df18ebe6-0568-442c-a4d2-445ab9c9412f` |
| Naming | Feed Naming Standard | FN-13 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_e892add5-96e7-42e6-a7b3-47cce066c4ef` |
| Output location | Landing Zone Layout | LZ-14 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_eaccf456-16d4-4567-b9cf-6f3473171368` |
| Storage & retention | Storage Tier Register | ST-16 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_dbe5d08a-5e3d-4b92-b4a1-6f33190122e1` |
| Capacity | Procurement Commitment Ledger | PV-25 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_019c6f62-9c9e-412d-8953-0b2c0000ed8f` |
| Landing time & lateness | Delivery Expectation Standard | LH-18 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_927e91ab-6739-4648-be8f-498c4178a64d` |
| Re-runs | Feed Re-run Procedure | RP-22 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_acda6d67-c604-4ca5-9f01-f3297e871e2e` |

| Covering instruments | Data Sharing Agreement Register | SA-27 | `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_23d185f0-2e62-4f16-8bc9-deeac019c77c` |

---

## 9. Standing-up sequence

Drawn from the standards above; each step is an obligation one of them imposes before the feed can be relied on.

1. **Fix the name** as `invoice-adjustments` under FN-13, and confirm the output carries the same name.
2. **Create the single prefix** `invoice-adjustments` in the landing area under LZ-14, partitioned by write date, with write access limited to the feed.

7. **Before any off-platform copy is contemplated**, confirm with the legal office that a live SA-27 entry covers this feed's record categories and the intended purpose; file the EG-24 approval before the copy.

# Change Plan — Adding a Field to `orders-ledger` Records

**Prepared for:** the owner of the `orders-ledger` producing service
**Date prepared:** 2026-08-10
**Change:** add one new field to the records carried on the `orders-ledger` stream
**Basis:** the platform's recorded knowledge pages, cited inline. Nothing below is drawn from general practice; where the recorded material is silent, this document says so rather than filling the gap.

---

## 1. Standing facts that drive this plan

`orders-ledger` carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from. It is a **governed-tier** stream: its records feed the statutory accounts, so how it changes is bound by the governed-tier obligations rather than by the producing team's own judgment (*Orders Ledger Stream Runbook*, `mcp:knowledge_page:kp_6bf7122a-f2cc-498f-aa3b-12e2635c88bd`).

Three consequences follow immediately, and they set the shape of everything below:

1. **The owner cannot classify this change themselves, and cannot waive the classification** (*Governed Tier Obligations*, `kp_404dc85f-f3f9-43b4-8e8b-85145a5f1438`).
2. **The producing team does not announce the change.** Consumer-facing notices go out centrally (*Change Announcement Directory*, `kp_9d40e2d6-5e24-4c93-ad10-72b29108c2ab`).
3. **The producing team does not choose the date.** Timing observes the finance organization's close calendar (*Company Close Calendar*, `kp_1ef079e6-bd03-433a-a7eb-3c7eb4e4bd7e`).

### Instruments this change touches

| Instrument | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Class **RB-7** | Change class for incompatible record-shape changes, incl. a field added | *Change Class Directory* `kp_41340dae-…` |
| Mode **CM-3** | Compatibility mode `orders-ledger` sits in, checked at registration | *Schema Version Register* `kp_efc01258-…` |
| Bulletin **AN-5** | The consumer-facing change announcement | *Change Announcement Directory* `kp_9d40e2d6-…` |
| Agreement **CA-9** | Per-stream consumer registration; the notice boundary | *Consumer Agreement Ledger* `kp_3d3ca779-…` |
| Window **QW-4** | The close quiet window during which the change may not be applied | *Company Close Calendar* `kp_1ef079e6-…` |
| Form **AT-12** | The owner's post-change completeness attestation | *Attestation Procedure* `kp_4b6c8ab9-…` |
| Series **RR-21** | Retention series the issued bulletin is filed under | *Corporate Records Retention Directory* `kp_6427a48f-…` |

---

## 2. The design constraint you must satisfy before anything else

Two recorded rules both bite on an added field, and they do not say the same thing. Read them together before drafting the field:

- **The class directory treats a field addition as incompatible.** Class RB-7 explicitly covers "a field added, renamed, retyped or removed," and states that the class **does not shorten for changes the producer considers small: compatibility is judged from the consumer's side** (`kp_41340dae-…`).
- **The register will not accept a version that breaks existing readers.** `orders-ledger` sits in mode **CM-3, the strictest**: a new version must be **readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change**, and every proposed version is checked against that mode at registration time (`kp_efc01258-…`).

**What this means operationally:** the change must be designed so that a consumer reading the current version can read the new version unmodified — otherwise registration fails and there is no lawful path to production. Passing the CM-3 check does **not** downgrade the change out of RB-7; the class is set by what is done to the record shape, not by how gentle the result is. Plan for **both**: a CM-3-clean field design **and** the full RB-7 notice obligation.

The recorded material does not describe *how* CM-3 readability is demonstrated (optionality, defaults, a reader-compatibility test suite, a specific serialization discipline). That is an open item in §12; resolve it with whoever operates the register before drafting.

---

## 3. Approvals this change needs

The recorded material names four distinct approval or sign-off points. There is no single "change board" recorded.

| # | Approval | Who gives it | When | Recorded at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | **Classification of the change** | Not the owner — the owner "cannot waive a classification." The material does not name the classifying body. | Before any work begins | `kp_404dc85f-…` |
| A2 | **Registration approval of the new version** | Not named. The register entry "carries the version, the classification of the change that produced it, and **who approved it**," so an approver exists and is recorded. | At registration, before any producer writes the new shape | `kp_efc01258-…` |
| A3 | **Written agreement from the consuming side** — *conditional* | The owner of the consuming side. Required only if you seek anything lighter than the heavier reading of a class boundary, or (see §6) if you intend not to wait the full notice for a given consumer. | Before relying on the lighter treatment | `kp_41340dae-…`, `kp_3d3ca779-…` |
| A4 | **Written exception to apply during QW-4** — *conditional, avoid* | The controller's office. Granted in writing, and **treated as a finding in the close report**. | Only if the change cannot wait for statement sign-off | `kp_1ef079e6-…` |
| A5 | **AT-12 attestation** (a sign-off, not a permission) | The producing service's **named owner**, personally. Cannot be delegated below the named owner. | After the change is live and the first full settlement has passed | `kp_4b6c8ab9-…` |

**Vacancy rule:** if the named owner role is vacant, the vacancy **suspends changes** — it does not suspend the attestation (`kp_4b6c8ab9-…`). Confirm the named owner is in post before starting.

---

## 4. Rules that constrain *when* the change may be applied

1. **The RB-7 waiting period.** Consumers are owed **17 business days of advance notice before the change is applied**, counted **in the consuming teams' working calendar**. The clock **runs from the day the announcement is actually delivered** — not the day it was drafted, approved, or posted (`kp_41340dae-…`).
2. **The QW-4 quiet window.** The stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off is QW-4. During QW-4, systems whose figures flow into the statements are **left as they are**; production alterations wait until the books are signed. `orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, so it is squarely in scope. Exceptions exist only in writing from the controller's office and are recorded as close-report findings (`kp_1ef079e6-…`).
3. **Nothing writes an unregistered shape.** A record shape that reaches the stream unregistered **is an incident, not a shortcut** (`kp_efc01258-…`). Registration strictly precedes the first producer write of the new shape — including in any environment that writes to the real stream.
4. **Period dates are published, not assumed.** Period dates, cutoff times, and the current window's standing are published on the finance group's internal page **each period** (`kp_1ef079e6-…`). Check the live publication when scheduling; do not schedule off a remembered cadence.
5. **Day-to-day rhythm.** The stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning (`kp_6bf7122a-…`) — relevant to picking an apply time and to §9's settlement wait.

**Scheduling rule of thumb:** target an apply date that is (a) at least 17 business days after actual bulletin delivery, in the consumers' calendar, and (b) clear of QW-4 **with margin for the first full settlement afterwards**, since §9's attestation depends on a settlement completing.

---

## 5. What the stream's consumers are owed

Everything owed to consumers flows through two records: the **agreement ledger** (who is owed) and the **AN-5 bulletin** (what they get).

- **Who is owed anything.** Consumers are those with a registered **CA-9 agreement** for `orders-ledger`. Registration is a condition of read access and is also the **notice boundary**: a team that never registered **is owed nothing, however long it has been reading** (`kp_3d3ca779-…`). Pull the current CA-9 list for `orders-ledger` as the definitive distribution list — do not build a list from observed traffic or from memory.
- **What each agreement tells you.** A CA-9 names the consuming service, its owner, and **the fields it depends on** (`kp_3d3ca779-…`). Use the declared-fields column when working §6.
- **The notice itself.** An **AN-5 bulletin**, issued **centrally** — deliberately so that "no consumer's notice depends on which team is making the change." It is delivered to every consumer the agreement ledger lists **and posted against the stream's register entry**. Where a delivered copy and the register disagree, **the register copy is authoritative** (`kp_9d40e2d6-…`).
- **The waiting period.** 17 business days from actual delivery, per §4.1.
- **Agreement review.** Agreements **are reviewed when a stream's shape changes** (`kp_3d3ca779-…`). This review is itself an owed step, not optional housekeeping — run it as step 6 in §8.
- **Filing.** Issued bulletins are corporate correspondence filed under **series RR-21**, **with their delivery evidence, at the time of issue** — "filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought." Disposal is reviewed by the records office, not the issuing team (`kp_6427a48f-…`). Practically: capture per-consumer delivery evidence as the bulletin goes out, because the delivery date is also what starts the 17-day clock.

---

## 6. The one genuine ambiguity: may any consumer be *notified without being waited for*?

The agreement ledger says: "a consumer whose **declared fields are untouched** by a change may be notified **without being waited for**, at the announcing owner's discretion" (`kp_3d3ca779-…`).

An added field touches **no** existing declared field, so on a literal reading every registered consumer could be notified without a wait. But the class directory says RB-7's notice "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small" and that **compatibility is judged from the consumer's side**, and that where two classes are in doubt "the heavier one applies **until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing**" (`kp_41340dae-…`). The recorded material does not reconcile these two statements.

**Recommended handling, and what to execute as written:**

- **Default: wait the full 17 business days for every registered consumer.** This satisfies both readings.
- If you need to compress for a specific consumer, obtain that consumer's **owner's agreement in writing** (A3) and file it with the change record. Written consuming-side agreement is the one mechanism both pages recognise.
- Do **not** shorten the period for a consumer unilaterally on the strength of the ledger's discretion clause alone; the class directory's "judged from the consumer's side" language points the other way, and the owner cannot waive a classification.

---

## 7. Where the material is silent on the engineering work itself

The recorded pages govern classification, registration, announcement, timing, and attestation. They say **nothing** about:

- how the producer is built, tested, or staged before the apply date;
- any rollback or back-out procedure for a governed-stream change;
- backfill of the new field onto historical records;
- who updates consumer-facing documentation or the catalog (a catalog search for `orders-ledger` returned no catalog, governance, or context-document entries at all — see §12).

Do not invent these into the change record as if they were policy. Plan them with the producing team as ordinary engineering, and note in the change record that they were locally decided rather than governed.

---

## 8. The executable sequence

Steps are in strict order. Each names its gate.

**Phase 1 — Before any work begins**

1. **Confirm the named owner is in post.** A vacancy suspends changes (`kp_4b6c8ab9-…`). If vacant, stop here.
2. **Get the change classified** (A1). Submit the proposed field to whoever classifies governed-stream changes. Expect **RB-7** — a field added is named in the class. Record the classification; you cannot waive it. *Gate: no work begins before the class is set (`kp_404dc85f-…`).*
3. **Pull the CA-9 list** for `orders-ledger` from the agreement ledger: every registered consumer, its owner, and its declared fields (`kp_3d3ca779-…`). This is your distribution list and your notice boundary.
4. **Read the current close calendar publication** for period dates, journal cutoff, and the current QW-4 standing (`kp_1ef079e6-…`).

**Phase 2 — Design and registration**

5. **Design the field to pass CM-3**: readable by every consumer of the current version **without a code change** (`kp_efc01258-…`). Confirm the demonstration method with the register operators (see §12).
6. **Run the agreement review** the ledger requires when a stream's shape changes (`kp_3d3ca779-…`). Record, per consumer, whether its declared fields are touched. Feed the result into §6.
7. **Register the new version** against the schema version register (A2). The entry carries the version, the RB-7 classification, and the approver. *Gate: registration precedes any producer write of the new shape, anywhere that reaches the stream — an unregistered shape on the stream is an incident (`kp_efc01258-…`).*

**Phase 3 — Announcement and the waiting period**

8. **Request the AN-5 bulletin** through the central announcement route — the producing team does not announce directly (`kp_6bf7122a-…`, `kp_9d40e2d6-…`). The bulletin must go to every CA-9-registered consumer and be **posted against the register entry**, which is the authoritative copy.
9. **Capture delivery evidence per consumer at issue**, and file the bulletin under **RR-21 with that evidence at the time of issue** (`kp_6427a48f-…`).
10. **Start the clock from the actual delivery date** and count **17 business days in the consuming teams' working calendar** (`kp_41340dae-…`). Where consumers keep different calendars, the latest-clearing consumer sets the earliest lawful apply date.
11. **Handle any compression case** per §6 — written consuming-owner agreement only, filed with the change record.
12. **Verify the register copy and the delivered copy agree.** If they differ, the register copy governs (`kp_9d40e2d6-…`); correct the discrepancy before applying.

**Phase 4 — Applying the change**

13. **Re-check QW-4 immediately before applying.** If the books are closing — journal cutoff has passed and the statements are not signed — **wait** (`kp_1ef079e6-…`). Seek a controller's-office exception only if the change genuinely cannot wait, accepting that it lands as a finding in the close report (A4).
14. **Confirm the earliest lawful date is met on both counts** — notice period elapsed *and* outside QW-4 — then apply the change, producing the registered version and nothing else. The **announced scope is what may be delivered** (`kp_4b6c8ab9-…`); do not slip a second field in with the first.
15. **Watch the overnight settle and the morning lag review** (`kp_6bf7122a-…`). If settlement reconciliation starts failing, go to §10 before anything else.

**Phase 5 — Closing the change**

16. **Wait for the first full settlement to pass** (`kp_4b6c8ab9-…`).
17. **File form AT-12**, signed personally by the named owner (A5), stating that:
    - the records now flowing **match the registered version**;
    - **no consumer-visible field was dropped** along the way;
    - **the announced scope is the delivered scope**.
18. **Confirm the change is closed in the tier's books.** An unattested change "is treated as unfinished however long it has been live" and is raised at every review until the form is filed (`kp_404dc85f-…`, `kp_4b6c8ab9-…`). The change is not done at deploy; it is done at AT-12.

---

## 9. Definition of done

The field is live **and** all of the following hold:

- a register entry exists carrying the new version, the RB-7 classification, and the named approver;
- an AN-5 bulletin was delivered to every CA-9-registered consumer, posted against the register entry, and filed under RR-21 with its delivery evidence;
- 17 business days elapsed between actual delivery and apply (or written consuming-owner agreement is on file for each compressed consumer);
- the apply fell outside QW-4, or a written controller's-office exception is on file;
- the agreement review of affected CA-9s is recorded;
- **AT-12 is filed and signed personally by the named owner.**

---

## 10. Contingency: if the change disturbs settlement agreement

`orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, and the nightly **settlement-recon** job agrees the day's settlement records against processor statements (`kp_07d3bb3e-…`). If the change destabilises that agreement, the following is not the owner's to improvise:

- **One failed night** is watched; **two** are worked during the day; **a third consecutive failed night opens an IN-28 incident record** — the unagreed days now span a statement cycle (`kp_07d3bb3e-…`).
- **Severity is set by the standard, not by the team that opened it.** A reconciliation or settlement control failing across a statement cycle is **band SB-8**, which notifies the owning team and the platform group's shift lead at opening and escalates along the **garnet route** (`kp_e2c59c5d-…`).
- **Garnet route:** platform shift lead → duty manager → head of platform operations, one rung at a time, never skipping a rung that has acknowledged. Settlement-family clocks: **first rung 23 minutes, second rung 34 minutes, final rung holds until answered.** Under rule **AC-15**, an expired clock advances the call on its own and the missed rung is recorded as missed (`kp_f2e9f42c-…`, `kp_a5108df2-…`).
- **Communications** follow cadence **UC-11**: the opening notice names the affected control, the days in question, and when the next update arrives; every update reports progress or honestly re-promises the next time. **Narrowing the audience mid-incident is not permitted**, and missing an update is itself reportable (`kp_1067fb7b-…`).
- **Regulatory overlay:** if the failure falls inside a statutory filing window, notification follows the compliance office's calendar. Form **RN-26** is lodged with the filing **before the window closes**, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand. **Word arriving after lodgment becomes a correction, which regulators treat differently** (`kp_e2c59c5d-…`, `kp_34127358-…`).
- **Closure requires evidence, not silence:** a **CE-2** record of the control passing **on its own schedule, unassisted**, with the previously unagreed days brought current. A manually forced pass does not qualify; a quiet night with the control disabled qualifies less. CE-2 attaches to the incident **before** the closing notice, which goes to the full audience and names the evidence (`kp_34843ea5-…`, `kp_1067fb7b-…`).
- **After closure:** a **PM-6 review record** — timeline of the nights, originating conditions as actually understood, corrections **each with a named owner**, and the review meeting's outcome. A record whose corrections have no owner is returned rather than filed, and it is referenced from the control's own operating notes (`kp_fd11860f-…`). Hours worked outside the working day on those nights are entered by hand under code **TL-19** with date and one-line purpose, **before the following week's payroll cutoff**, and must be entered **before the PM-6 is filed** — an unentered line lapses (`kp_56d1ed1a-…`).

Note that this branch would leave the change both live and disruptive while AT-12 is still owed; §8 step 18 still applies.

---

## 11. One side-condition worth flagging

If, during the notice period, the owner shares sample records or extracts of the new shape with a consumer **outside the platform**, that is a copy of feed output and carries an **EG-24 approval** naming the receiving party, the purpose, and the deletion date — an approval missing any of the three is returned unactioned — plus a covering instrument looked up in the legal office's data sharing agreement register (`kp_68af16b8-…`, `kp_23d185f0-…`). Keep worked examples on-platform and this does not arise.

---

## 12. Open items

Each of the following is something this plan needs and the available material does not record. None can be resolved from what the platform holds today.

1. **Who classifies the change (A1).** The obligations page says the owner cannot classify or waive; it does not name the body that does, or how a classification is requested.
2. **Who approves a registered version (A2).** The register entry records "who approved it," but no page states which role holds that authority or what the approval submission looks like.
3. **How CM-3 readability is demonstrated.** The register checks every version against the mode "at registration time," but the check's method, evidence, and failure path are not recorded.
4. **Whether RB-7 and CM-3 can both be satisfied for a field addition, and by whom that is confirmed.** The class explicitly names "a field added" as incompatible, while CM-3 demands no-code-change readability. §2 assumes both must hold simultaneously; nothing recorded confirms or denies it.
5. **How the CA-9 "notify without waiting" discretion interacts with RB-7's fixed 17 days.** §6 recommends the conservative reading; the pages do not reconcile them.
6. **Whether the delivery day counts as day 1** of the 17 business days. The class directory says the notice "runs from the day the announcement is actually delivered" without stating inclusivity.
7. **Which working calendar applies per consumer.** Counting is "in the consuming teams' working calendar," but the CA-9 record as described names the service, its owner, and declared fields — not a calendar.
8. **The identity of the stream's owning team and its named owner.** The runbook refers to "the stream's owning team" and AT-12 to "the producing service's named owner"; no page names either, and no catalog entry for `orders-ledger` exists to carry ownership metadata.
9. **The current registered consumer list for `orders-ledger`.** The ledger's rules are recorded; its contents are not available through the platform to me.
10. **Current period dates, journal cutoff, and QW-4 standing.** Published on the finance group's internal page each period; not reachable from here.
11. **Where AN-5, CA-9, AT-12, and the register itself physically live** — the systems, forms, or queues used to file and retrieve them.
12. **The RR-21 retention period.** The directory says items are kept "for the period the directory lists for the series"; the period is not stated on the page.
13. **Whether AT-12's "first full settlement" means the nightly settlement-recon job.** The runbook describes that job and the stream's overnight settle, but no page states that this is the settlement AT-12 waits on. §8 step 16 assumes it is; confirm before relying on the timing.
14. **Rollback, staging, backfill, and consumer documentation.** No recorded procedure exists for backing out a governed-stream change, for testing the new shape before the apply date, for backfilling the new field onto historical records, or for updating catalog/field documentation — and no catalog, governance, or context-document entry for `orders-ledger` was found at all, so there is no recorded place for field-level documentation to go.
